changes_from_1995.Ng ng: no longer a separate letter; spelled n+g as before

contextual.е: 'ye' at word start, after a vowel, after ъ or ь; otherwise 'e'
contextual.ц: 'ts' after a vowel; 's' at word start or after a consonant
contextual.ъ: dropped before е ё ю я (the iotated vowel supplies the y); dropped after ў when target is Latin (мўъжиза → moʻjiza); otherwise ʼ (U+02BC)
contextual.ь: always dropped (before е ё ю я the vowel supplies the y: компьютер → kompyuter)
contextual.с+ҳ: target lat: 'sʼh' (Исҳоқ → Isʼhoq) to prevent reading as 'sh'; target new: plain 'sh' (Ş exists, so s+h is unambiguous)

digraphs.sh: ш (source lat only; source new: с+ҳ)
digraphs.ye: е at word start / after vowel / after apostrophe; after a consonant: ье (dictionary overrides give ъе: obyekt → объект)
digraphs.yo: ё (but y + oʻ → йў: yoʻl → йўл)
digraphs.e: э at word start or after a vowel; е after a consonant
digraphs.apostrophe between letters: ъ (tutuq belgisi); word-final U+02BC → ъ; other stray apostrophes/quotes are left untouched

casing.rule: When a single source letter expands to several output letters (Ш→Sh, Ё→Yo, Ц→Ts, Е→Ye, Ş→Sh), use ALL CAPS if the source letter is uppercase AND its next letter is uppercase (or, with no next letter, its previous letter is uppercase); use Title case if only the source letter is uppercase; otherwise lowercase. Single-letter outputs simply copy the case of the source letter.
